categories.name: Education & Teaching

info.text: How people teach and learn: pedagogy, instructional design, assessment, curriculum, and training.

categories.rationale: TAXONOMY-ROADMAP deliberate gap (Education & Teaching). No education-teaching domain yet — use social-sciences until that domain is admitted. Do not register in categories.js until the first puzzle merges.

info.text: How learning is measured, judged, and used to guide teaching — from classroom checks to high-stakes exams.
How learning experiences are planned so goals, activities, and evidence of learning align.

categories.name: Law & Governance

info.text: Constitutional structure, rights, procedure, regulation, and international law — how rules bind institutions and people.

categories.rationale: TAXONOMY-ROADMAP reserved vocabulary. Promote when several authored puzzles clearly want it. Domain stays social-sciences until a dedicated law domain exists. Do not register empty.

info.text: How public power is allocated, limited, and reviewed — separation of powers, federalism, and judicial review.
How legal process and rights claims constrain state and private action.

seedSubjects: rule of law vs rule by law

categories.name: Religion

info.text: How communities make meaning through belief, practice, text, and institution — and how those forms shape ethics and identity.

categories.rationale: Standard humanities department; roadmap humanities scope includes religion. No registered home today. Do not register empty.

info.text: How religious communities read, interpret, and authorize texts as scripture.
How embodied practices — worship, pilgrimage, observance — structure religious life beyond belief alone.

categories.name: Physics

info.text: How matter and energy interact under general laws — from particles and fields to motion, waves, and thermodynamics.

categories.rationale: Course-catalog staple currently folded into generic Science. Promote as its own category when the first physics-first puzzle lands. Do not register empty.

info.text: How forces, energy, and momentum explain motion of everyday-scale objects.
How disturbances and continuous field quantities carry energy and information through space.

categories.name: Linguistics

info.text: How human language is structured and used: sound, form, meaning, and variation across speakers and communities.

categories.rationale: Distinct from Language Arts (rhetoric/composition craft). Standard departmental subject. Do not register empty.

info.text: How languages organize sound systems and build words from smaller meaningful parts.
How words combine into sentences and how those structures map to meaning.

categories.name: Architecture

info.text: How built form organizes space, structure, use, and experience — from rooms and materials to cities.

categories.rationale: Institutional home between Art & Design and Engineering; not covered by Film or Art visual-form. Do not register empty.

info.text: How enclosure, sequence, light, and proportion shape how people move through and read buildings.
How load paths and material properties constrain what can be built and how it stands.

subcategories.title: Marketing

info.text: How organizations find, persuade, and keep customers — and what that reveals about value and attention.

subcategories.rationale: Course-catalog staple under a thin parent. Register only with the first marketing puzzle.

subcategories.title: International Relations

info.text: How states and non-state actors cooperate, compete, and govern across borders.

subcategories.rationale: Common departmental slice without inventing a new top-level category.

subcategories.title: Behavioral Economics

info.text: How psychology revises classical models of choice — bias, heuristics, and institutions that work with them.

subcategories.rationale: Fits existing Economics grain; opens a clear course-catalog slice.

subcategories.rationale: Prefer a Math subcategory over a separate Statistics category.

info.text: How designed systems sense, decide, and act under feedback and constraint — beyond electronics alone.

subcategories.rationale: Parent currently has only electronics; this opens the systems half of the category brief.

subcategories.title: Music Theory

info.text: How pitch, rhythm, harmony, and form are organized so music can be heard as structure.

subcategories.rationale: Thin parent; formalizes the theory slice already implied by category copy.

info.text: How medical care raises questions of consent, vulnerability, trust, and harm that clinical facts alone don't settle.

subcategories.rationale: Parent currently has no subcategories at all. Candidate puzzle: accretive-health-scandal (parked, not yet submitted) — register only if/when it or another bioethics-first puzzle actually lands.
